app.title: Protein Sequence Analyzer
app.summary: A person pastes one protein sequence, either as plain letters or as a FASTA record, and clicks Analyze. The sequence is checked first: nucleotide-only input and letters that are not amino acids are rejected, and very short or very long sequences get a warning. The results are split across tabs: a dashboard of physicochemical properties with a radar profile, a per-residue composition table with charts, predicted secondary-structure fractions with a hydrophobic/hydrophilic split, and a tab of plain-language interpretations. The last tab also lets the person download the property table as CSV, Excel or JSON, and a PDF report.

task.text: Compute a physicochemical property profile for one protein sequence, interpret it with fixed rules, and export it as a table or report.

data.text: A single amino-acid sequence, and the table of properties computed from it.
data.item: one protein sequence, pasted as raw letters or as a single FASTA record

stage.text: analyzing a protein sequence's computed properties, after the sequence is known

mechanism.text: One paste box and an Analyze button check the sequence and compute every property at once. Four tabs then show the results as metric tiles, a radar chart, tables and bar charts, and rule-based text, and download buttons save the same property table in several formats.

field.text: physicochemical protein sequence characterization in bioinformatics

workflow.name: compute a property profile for one item and export it as a report

steps.here: The sequence is pasted into a text area as raw letters or as FASTA. Clicking Analyze Protein reads the FASTA header if there is one, removes spaces and line breaks, and converts the letters to upper case.

steps.step: check the input is valid before computing
steps.here: Input made only of DNA or RNA bases is rejected, any letter outside the 20 amino acids is listed as invalid, and a warning appears below 20 or above 5000 residues.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Molecular weight, pI, instability index, GRAVY, aromaticity and the reduced and oxidized extinction coefficients are shown as metric tiles and a normalized radar chart. The tab also shows the sequence ID, a residue summary and a 100-residue preview.

steps.step: break the item down by category
steps.here: A table and bar charts give the count and percentage of each residue type. Residues are also pooled into hydrophobic and hydrophilic groups, and the helix, turn and sheet fractions are charted along with the one that dominates.

Fixed rules turn each property into a statement: stability from the instability index, solubility from the hydrophobic share, the dominant secondary structure, disulfide bonds from the gap between the extinction coefficients, and an overall assessment.
The property table can be downloaded as CSV, Excel or JSON, and a formatted PDF report can be downloaded as well.

distinctive: Nucleotide sequences are detected and rejected, so only amino-acid input reaches the calculations.
An instability index below 40 is the field's rule for calling a protein stable, and this verdict appears in the dashboard, the interpretation and the reports.
The reduced and oxidized extinction coefficients are compared to predict whether disulfide bonds affect UV absorbance at 280 nm.
Six properties with different units are each scaled to 0–1 over a fixed range so they fit on one radar chart.
Residues are split into hydrophobic and hydrophilic using a fixed list, and the result is read as likely membrane-associated or likely soluble.

parts.title: Sequence input and validation
parts.summary: Takes a pasted raw or FASTA protein sequence, parses it, and either rejects it with the reason or passes it on to analysis.

parts.title: Basic Analysis tab
parts.summary: Shows the protein's core physicochemical properties, a summary table, the extinction coefficients and a stability verdict.

parts.title: Protein dashboard and radar chart
parts.summary: Shows the main properties as metric tiles, then draws them scaled 0–1 on a radar chart so the protein's profile can be seen at a glance.

parts.title: FASTA information
parts.summary: Lists the sequence ID and description, its length, how many distinct residues it has and the most common one, and shows a preview of the sequence.

parts.title: Amino Acid Composition tab
parts.summary: Gives the count and percentage of each amino acid as a table and as two bar charts.

parts.title: Structural Analysis tab
parts.summary: Charts the predicted helix, turn and sheet fractions and the hydrophobic/hydrophilic split, each with a one-line reading.

parts.title: Interpretation tab
parts.summary: Turns the computed properties into plain-language statements using fixed thresholds, and ends with an overall assessment.

parts.title: Download center
parts.summary: Shows the full property table and offers it as CSV, Excel or JSON, plus a formatted PDF report.
